title: Documentary Photography
description: The unflinching photograph — the FSA archive and the pioneers of the form.

items.title: Migrant Mother
items.description_narrative: A careworn woman rests her chin on her hand, brow furrowed, as two children turn their faces into her shoulders and an infant sleeps in her lap. Dorothea Lange photographed Florence Owens Thompson on 6 March 1936; the portrait now hangs in museum collections nationwide.
items.tags: portrait, mother and children, depression era, dorothea lange, black and white, documentary
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8b29516.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Toward Los Angeles
items.description_narrative: Two men walk away from the camera along a dirt shoulder beside a highway, one carrying a suitcase and the other a bundled pack. Beside them a billboard urges travelers to try the train instead, its cheerful painted figure at odds with the men's slow, dusty progress. Dorothea Lange made the photograph in March 1937.
items.tags: photography, migration, great depression, black and white, road, documentary
items.credit_line: LOC Flickr Commons restoration, LC-DIG-fsa-8b31801; supersedes the earlier TIF-decode-broken edit

items.title: Tractored Out, Childress County Texas
items.cultural_context: American documentary photography, Great Depression era
items.description_narrative: Deep plow furrows curve across an empty field toward a small, abandoned farmhouse standing alone beneath a flat, featureless sky. Dorothea Lange photographed this tenantless farm in the Texas panhandle in June 1938.
items.tags: dust bowl, abandoned farmhouse, plowed field, black and white, dorothea lange, rural america
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsc.00232.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: The Steerage
items.description_narrative: Passengers crowd a ship's upper deck behind a chain railing, hats and shawls pressed close together, while more travelers wait below near a gangplank and ladder. Alfred Stieglitz photographed the scene aboard the SS Kaiser Wilhelm II in 1907, a landmark image of early modernist photography.
items.tags: steerage, ship deck, immigrants, black and white, alfred stieglitz, modernism
items.credit_line: DwGsXk0l3l7fkw at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Floyd Burroughs, cotton sharecropper
items.description_narrative: A man in patched overalls and a worn cotton shirt sits close to the camera, his weathered face turned toward the lens with a steady, unsmiling gaze. Walker Evans's gelatin silver print is a close portrait, the wood-plank wall behind him left in deep shadow.
items.tags: portrait, photography, black and white, great depression, sharecropper, documentary
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8c52247.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Allie Mae Burroughs
items.cultural_context: American, Great Depression era, Documentary Photography
items.description_narrative: A woman stands squarely before weathered clapboard siding, her dark hair parted and combed close, a small patterned housedress buttoned to the throat. Her steady, unsmiling gaze meets the camera directly. Walker Evans made this portrait in 1936.
items.tags: portrait, rural south, black and white, walker evans, depression era, direct gaze
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8c52248.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: American Gothic, Washington, D.C.
items.description_narrative: A woman in glasses and a polka-dot dress stands with a broom in one hand and a mop propped beside her, a large American flag hanging in soft folds behind her. Gordon Parks made this photograph in August 1942.
items.tags: portrait, broom, american flag, gordon parks, black and white, documentary
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8b14845.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.
items.current_repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division

items.title: Power house mechanic working on steam pump
items.cultural_context: Social documentary photography, Early 20th Century American
items.description_narrative: A shirtless young mechanic braces against a massive riveted pump housing, gripping a heavy wrench as he leans into the machinery around him. Lewis Hine photographed this power house worker in 1920.
items.tags: industrial labor, machinery, black and white, lewis hine, mechanic, documentary
items.credit_line: https://web.archive.org/web/20221204115953/https://www.archives.gov/exhibits/picturing_the_century/portfolios/port_hine.html links to hi-res image) Image is not currently (as of 2007-03-22) in the ARC catalog. File 69-RH is available under ARC identifier 518289 (search at https://arcweb.archives.gov/arc/basic_search.jsp), but it currently only contains a single photo (ARC identifier 518290, item 69-RH-4K-1).

items.title: Breaker Boys, Pennsylvania
items.description_narrative: Boys in flat caps crouch and sit among wooden chutes and iron pipes, packed shoulder to shoulder inside a coal breaker, one jacket hanging forgotten on a post nearby. Lewis Hine documented these child laborers in 1911.
items.tags: child labor, coal mining, black and white, lewis hine, industrial, documentary
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID nclc.05473.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Spinner in a Cotton Mill
items.description_narrative: A young girl stands between long rows of spinning frames, bobbins bristling on either side of her, threads and scraps scattered on the floor at her feet. Lewis Hine photographed her at the Globe Cotton Mill in Augusta, Georgia, in January 1909.
items.tags: child labor, cotton mill, textile industry, black and white, lewis hine, documentary
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID nclc.01641.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Bandit's Roost
items.description_narrative: Men in hats and jackets fill a narrow alley strung overhead with drying laundry, some posed on stoops, others leaning against the walls that press in on both sides. Jacob Riis photographed this Mulberry Street alley in 1888.
items.tags: alley, tenement, street photography, black and white, jacob riis, new york

items.title: Ancient Ruins in the Canyon de Chelly
items.description_narrative: Tiny masonry ruins nestle in the shadow of an immense, streaked sandstone wall, dwarfed by the scale of the canyon around them. Timothy H. O'Sullivan photographed this site, known as the 'White House' ruin, in 1873.
items.tags: canyon, ancient ruins, sandstone cliff, sepia, timothy o'sullivan, american southwest
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsca.10055.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Yosemite Valley from Inspiration Point
items.description_narrative: Steep granite walls rise on either side of a forested valley, a thin waterfall threading down a distant cliff face, pine trees and boulders filling the foreground. Carleton Watkins made this negative around 1865.
items.tags: yosemite, valley, granite cliffs, waterfall, sepia, carleton watkins
items.credit_line: 6wHjXKTSmvR6Hg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Boulevard du Temple
items.description_narrative: A wide tree-lined boulevard curves away beneath rows of tall apartment buildings, its cobbled surface and rooftops rendered in soft, grainy tones. Louis Daguerre made this street view around 1838.
items.tags: cityscape, boulevard, daguerreotype, sepia, paris, early photography
items.credit_line: Scanned from The Photography Book, Phaidon Press, London, 1997.

items.title: The Open Door
items.medium: Salted paper print from a calotype negative
items.description_narrative: A broom leans against a weathered wooden doorway left ajar, a shadowed interior beyond, while a vine climbs the stone wall and a small vessel hangs from a hook nearby. William Henry Fox Talbot made this study in 1844.
items.tags: doorway, still life, sepia, calotype, william henry fox talbot, early photography

items.title: View from the Window at Le Gras
items.description_narrative: Rooftops slope away beneath a hazy sky in this rough, grainy view from an upper window, its forms softened almost to abstraction by the crude process that captured them. Joseph Nicéphore Niépce made this exposure in 1826.
items.tags: rooftops, sepia, early photography, heliograph, niepce, grainy
items.credit_line: Rebecca A. Moss,Director of Visual Resources and Digital Content Lab, via email. College of Liberal Arts Office of Information Technology University of Minnesota http://www.arthist.umn.edu/vrcinfo/

items.title: Geronimo
items.description_narrative: An elderly man wrapped in a heavy blanket wears an ornately beaded, disc-crowned cap, holding a long staff at his side as he regards the camera with a weathered, direct expression. Edward S. Curtis made this portrait in 1905.
items.tags: portrait, native american, sepia, edward curtis, regalia, historical photography
